overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Husserl's analysis of the intentional act. You'll be asked about act quality and matter, noesis and noema, adumbrations, and the two main readings of the noema.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Judging that it will rain tomorrow and wishing that it will rain tomorrow differ in what respect?

options.html: They share an act matter but differ in act quality
options.text: They share an act matter but differ in act quality
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both acts are directed at rain tomorrow, so they share a matter. Judging and wishing are different kinds of act, so they differ in quality.

options.html: They share an act quality but differ in act matter
options.text: They share an act quality but differ in act matter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Judging and wishing are different kinds of act, so they differ in quality. They're both directed at rain tomorrow, so they share a matter.

options.html: They differ in both act quality and act matter
options.text: They differ in both act quality and act matter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both acts are directed at rain tomorrow, so they share a matter. They differ only in quality: judging vs. wishing.

options.html: They share both act quality and act matter
options.text: They share both act quality and act matter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Judging and wishing are different kinds of act, so the acts differ in quality, though they share a matter: rain tomorrow.

options.html: The mental act of perceiving, remembering, or imagining
options.text: The mental act of perceiving, remembering, or imagining
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That describes the noesis, the act side. The noema is the object as meant, exactly as the act intends it.

options.html: A mental picture of the object stored in consciousness
options.text: A mental picture of the object stored in consciousness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. On any reading, the noema isn't a mental picture. It's the object as meant, exactly as the act intends it.

options.html: The object as meant, exactly as the act intends it
options.text: The object as meant, exactly as the act intends it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The noema is the object side of an intentional experience: the object as meant, such as the tree as seen from here.

options.html: The physical cause of the sensations in the act
options.text: The physical cause of the sensations in the act
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The noema isn't a cause. It's the object as meant, exactly as the act intends it.

forms.stemHtml: What is the English term for the profiles (Abschattungen) through which a perceived physical thing is given one side at a time?

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A perceived thing is given through adumbrations, profiles that present it from one side at a time, and never completely.
Correct! A perceived thing is given through adumbrations, profiles that present it from one side at a time, and never completely.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Husserl's Abschattungen are rendered in English as adumbrations: profiles through which a perceived thing is given one side at a time.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are claims of the Fregean reading of the noema? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The noema generalizes Frege's notion of sense to all intentional acts
options.text: The noema generalizes Frege's notion of sense to all intentional acts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Føllesdal proposed that the noema extends Frege's Sinn from language to every act.

options.html: The act is directed at its object by way of the noema
options.text: The act is directed at its object by way of the noema
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! On the Fregean reading, the noema mediates between act and object, as a sense mediates between an expression and its referent.

options.html: The noema is the object itself, considered just as it's meant
options.text: The noema is the object itself, considered just as it's meant
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the perceptual, or object, reading, defended by Sokolowski and Drummond.

options.html: The noema is a mental picture located inside the mind
options.text: The noema is a mental picture located inside the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Neither reading treats the noema as a mental picture. The Fregean reading treats it as an abstract sense.

forms.stemHtml: What does the choice between the two readings of the noema decide?

options.html: Whether perception gives its objects through adumbrations
options.text: Whether perception gives its objects through adumbrations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both readings accept adumbrations. The debate decides whether phenomenology is a theory of mental representation.

options.html: Whether phenomenology is a theory of mental representation
options.text: Whether phenomenology is a theory of mental representation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! On the Fregean reading, the noema plays the role of a mediating content, so phenomenology is a theory of representation. On the perceptual reading, it describes how objects appear.

options.html: Whether act quality and act matter can vary independently
options.text: Whether act quality and act matter can vary independently
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both readings accept that. The debate decides whether phenomenology is a theory of mental representation.

options.html: Whether the epoché should be applied to perception
options.text: Whether the epoché should be applied to perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The noema debate concerns what the noema is. It decides whether phenomenology is a theory of mental representation.

title: Noesis and Noema
